reason: The format list is exactly my daily stuff (TGA, DDS, EXR, HDR, GLB/OBJ/FBX, cbz) so I will install the portable zip and throw my own files at it. But it is 0.4.1 from one person and ImageGlass is open source, so I will not make it my default until it proves itself.
why_switch_or_not: 26 of 32 formats vs ImageGlass 17 is a real draw, and having 3D models, EXR and cbz in one viewer with a gallery, batch convert and an editor is how I like my tools. But a one-dev 0.4.1 with no plug-in system and nothing said about source being open means I could lose it if the dev gets bored, and I would not trust it to be my file association until my own DDS/TGA/EXR files open correctly. Speed numbers are nice but ImageGlass is not slow enough for me to switch for speed alone.
current_app_pros: ImageGlass looks modern, is open source, free, and handles the common formats and my cbz reading fine. It is stable and I know where everything is.
current_app_pains: It opens fewer of my formats (no real 3D models, some game textures and EXR/HDR are hit and miss), it is a bit slow on big files and when flipping through folders, and it is a viewer only, so I still bounce to other apps to convert or batch rename.
objection: Another image viewer from a single developer at version 0.4.1. Mine already works fine, and if it is abandoned or buggy on my game textures I have wasted the switch.
would_change_my_mind: Proof that my own DDS (compressed types, mip levels), TGA with alpha and multi-layer EXR open correctly, plus either the source being open or a clear track record of updates over several months.
